# BMW Challenge: AI for Product Decision Making

An AI-powered application that helps BMW product managers (PMs) derive, justify and prioritize customer requirements for a **successor vehicle**, with the PM in control of every decision. This folder is the knowledge base: the challenge, the provided data (raw and processed), what BMW people told us, and our own notes.

> **Agents:** start with [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md). It has the reading order, ground rules and where each kind of fact lives.

## Quick facts
- **Task:** concept + working prototype that turns heterogeneous inputs into prioritized, evidence-backed, customer-facing requirements, with human review and a full audit trail.
- **Vehicles:** 1 Series (F70), 5 Series (G60, China G68), 7 Series (G70). **Markets:** Europe, China, US (any subset). **Horizon:** 3 to 5 years.
- **Must deliver:** (1) prototype, (2) sample requirement list with ID, description, findings and sources, score, rationale, evidence level, assumptions and status, (3) end-to-end workflow with AI and human boundaries, (4) audit trail.
- **Judged on:** scoring logic, workflow and human decisions, traceability, usability and feasibility, innovation and scalability. **Honesty about uncertainty is rewarded.**
- **Out of scope:** regulation and homologation, engineering specs, pricing and business case (cost only as a rough factor).
- **Biggest data caveat:** no customer feedback from China; G60/G70 feedback is 90 to 95% US; F70 is UK/Japan and ICE only.

## Map

```
BMW-Challenge/
├── CLAUDE.md                 Agent entry point: reading order, rules, where to find what
├── GLOSSARY.md               Model codes, BMW/process terms, German option-list terms
├── 01-challenge/             What we are asked to build, and what BMW wants
├── 02-data/                  Provided BMW data: raw/, processed/ (CSV), insights, equipment
├── 03-meetings/              Meeting summaries (raw/ holds the transcripts)
├── 04-team-notes/            Our own brainstorming
└── 05-solution/              Our solution design: scope/focus, end-to-end flow, UX decisions
```

### 01-challenge: the task
| File | Content |
|---|---|
| [`hackathon-briefing.md`](01-challenge/hackathon-briefing.md) / [`.pdf`](01-challenge/hackathon-briefing.pdf) | Official brief: challenge, mission, what to demonstrate (the .md matches the 2-page PDF) |

# Argon (web)

The clickable demo of our BMW hackathon tool: **Signals → Cases → Requirements → Vehicle plan**. It runs on synthetic data behind a real REST contract, so the team can work in three tracks at once and replace the mock backend later with no UI changes.

- **Signal:** one piece of evidence with its source. Either a real BMW record (verbatim, study row) or a web finding (synthetic in the demo).
- **Case:** a customer problem built from signals. It has an importance score but no cost. The PM works it with open questions, meeting notes and Argus, the AI assistant, then decides one of: confirm, refer, innovation pool, park, merge or reject.
- **Requirement:** what BMW builds, created from a confirmed case. It carries a SMART text, measurable targets, a release (next generation, mid-life update or OTA) and a rough cost. It moves from draft through discussion and PM approval to head sign-off, then the vehicle plan, then Codebeamer export.

## Screens (six, after Thomas's "less is more" feedback)

| Nav | What the PM does there |
|---|---|
| **My desk** | Four cards sorted by kind of work: *Agent flags* (competitor alerts, @mentions) · *My cases* · *Review* (requirements sent back or in progress; for the head: regional brief differences, sign-off and escalations inline) · *Follow up* (answers that came back, questions due) |
| **Inbox** | Referrals to accept or decline, agent flags, all notifications |
| **Cases** | Kanban (drag = state change with a reason). A *Ranked* toggle shows the score order; weights sit behind one button |
| **Vehicle plan** | All requirements of a series as a list grouped by car area, with status filter chips, plan action and release; today's equipment folds per area; Codebeamer export |
| **Signals** | One Sankey: sources → car areas → cases. Click a node to see its signals and start a case from loose ones. *Refresh* plays the agent run step by step (fetch → classify → gate → match metrics → assess impact) |
| **Innovation pool** | Ideas parked for a future series; vote or pull into your series |

Three things borrowed from the market (see the competitor research):
- **Quality check on every requirement** (like Raiqon and Polarion run inside Codebeamer): vague wording, scope vs. evidence, out-of-scope content (regulatory, technical, pricing), duplicates, conflicting targets and Baukasten overlap. Rules always run; with an LLM key an AI pass adds issues. It warns but never blocks: *Approve as PM* lists the open issues and the reason is logged.
- **Ask the segment** in the case chat (like Dovetail's digital twins, but grounded): chips such as *USA (24) · USA BEV (9) · China (0)* answer only from that segment's real BMW verbatims, with citations. No verbatims means "no evidence" plus a proposed open question, never a guess.
- **Engineering deck** next to *Export to Codebeamer* (like Aha! roadmap decks): one slide per signed-off or planned requirement with the SMART text, three customer quotes, the score breakdown, the competition and the decision log.

A **case** opens with a Sankey of its evidence (*sources → what they say → case*, where "what they say" is a taxonomy topic × type, e.g. *Public charging · hard to use*). Every node is clickable and shows its quotes. Then three steps: **① Evidence** (Sankey + three bullets, full analysis on demand) → **② Your stance** (brief values you inherit, overridable with a reason; your take on the evidence; what you know that the data can't show; how far to go. Argus, the AI assistant, answers with follow-up questions; open questions to engineering and finance) → **③ Requirements** (up to three shape questions with defaults, then the draft in a side panel). Settings, the audit trail and **My series brief** live in the persona menu.

### PM context layers (why a draft reads like the PM wrote it)
The drafter combines five layers; [docs/05-solution/ux-and-collaboration.md](../docs/05-solution/ux-and-collaboration.md#5a-pm-context-layers-requirements-that-read-like-the-pm-wrote-them) has the design.

| Layer | UI | Budget |
|---|---|---|
| 0 Brand profile | Settings (head) | existing |
| 1 Series brief (shared + regional overlay) | `/brief`; onboarding on first login; *Paste your strategy doc* proposes values | ≤ 8 questions, pre-filled from data |
| 2 Case stance | step ② | 3 questions |
| 3 Shape questions | step ③ form, mirrored in the case chat | ≤ 3, each with a default and "why I'm asking" |
| 4 Engineering / finance feedback | *Engineering feedback* on a requirement → proposal for the next version | per round |

Every part of a drafted requirement shows where it came from (evidence with signal IDs, your context with the layer, or assumption). The **Versions** tab keeps the history on the same ID; a brief change shows the affected requirements and creates a version proposal per owner; a regional PM's variant shows a side-by-side "two briefs" comparison.

### Trace replay and the competitor ripple (no new nav item)
- **Trace replay** (*Replay* in the trace strip of every requirement, side panel and full page): a full-screen overlay plays the requirement's life in about 15 s. It opens on the requirement card, rewinds in 1 s to the first quote, then plays forward:
  1. voices: real BMW quotes with market and source; a sample of 12, all counted
  2. signals: topic × type nodes, each with its BMW label or model and prompt version
  3. case and score: the score built factor by factor under the weight profile active on the decision date, next to today's
  4. decisions: agent steps dashed with a bot icon, people solid with an avatar and their quoted reason
  5. planned: the vehicle-plan slot

  It ends in **Chain intact** with four checks recomputed on every call: every quote found in its source record, every record's SHA-256 matching, no gaps in the audit sequence, a rationale on every status change. A failed check shows in red with its reason. Esc closes, Space pauses, ←/→ step, 1×/2×, and a scrubber shows version, score and evidence as of any date. *Export dossier* downloads Markdown with the backend's `audit_chain.render` sections plus scores and integrity. Under `prefers-reduced-motion` the beats step without sweeps. The static Sankey with highlights is the base; the motion is layered on top.
- **Competitor ripple** (`/ripple/[id]`, opened from the Refresh toast, the agent flag on My desk, notifications and the alert strip on an affected requirement): a competitor fact with a metric is matched on `targetSpec.key` against every requirement target in the portfolio (all series, market variants, Baukasten). A competitor update affects requirements, not cases: a case without a requirement only carries the fact as evidence, and every competitor alert comes from a ripple. ```bash

Open http://localhost:3000 and pick a persona. The persona menu (top right) switches users and has **Reset demo data**.

| Script | What it does |
|---|---|
| `npm run dev` / `build` / `start` | Next.js 16 app plus the mock backend at `/api` |
| `npm run seed` | Rebuilds `src/mock/fixtures/seed.json` from the real CSVs in `All-context/02-data-provided-by-pm/processed/` plus the authored content. Validated against the contract |
| `npm run export-contract` | Writes `../contracts/openapi.yaml` and `../contracts/schemas/*.json` |
| `npm run contract-test` | Calls every endpoint against a running backend (`API_BASE`, default `http://localhost:3000/api`) and validates each response. Also walks the demo storyline |
| `npm run typecheck` / `lint` | Static checks |

Optional live AI chat: set `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` (optionally `LLM_MODEL`). Free-form chat questions then go to Claude with the case as context. Proposals, drafts and research stay scripted so they keep the contract. Without a key the scripted assistant answers offline. The team docs name OpenAI as the provider; to switch, change the single function in `src/mock/ai/live.ts`.

## How the code is split (three tracks)

```
contracts/                 (repo root) generated OpenAPI + JSON Schemas for the backend team
web/src/contracts/         Zod schemas = THE contract (enums, entities, endpoints, UI labels)
web/src/lib/api/           typed client (base URL: NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL, default /api) + TanStack Query hooks
web/src/app/(app)/         screens                                   ← frontend track
web/src/components/        UI building blocks (shadcn/ui in components/ui)
web/src/app/api/[...path]  MOCK BACKEND: one route implementing every endpoint   ← replaced by the backend track
web/src/mock/              in-memory store, reference scoring, scripted AI, seed fixtures   ← logic + data track
web/scripts/               seed, contract export, contract test
```

| Track | Owns | Works against |
|---|---|---|
| **Frontend** | `src/app/(app)`, `src/components` | `src/lib/api` hooks only (never imports `src/mock`) |
| **Backend / API** | A FastAPI service on Supabase (Ghassen's `data-model.mmd`) implementing `contracts/openapi.yaml` | `npm run contract-test` with `API_BASE=<their url>`; then set `NEXT_PUBLIC_API_BASE_URL` |
| **Logic + data** | Fetch agents, clustering, scoring, requirement drafting, chat/RAG, meeting-note extraction | The reference behaviour in `src/mock/scoring.ts`, `src/mock/ai/*` and the seed. Same inputs and outputs |

**Changing the contract:** edit `src/contracts/*.ts`, then run `npm run typecheck`, which shows every UI and mock spot to update. Then run `npm run export-contract` and commit `contracts/` so the backend sees the change.

**Rules the contract encodes (keep them in the real backend):**
- The acting user comes in as header `x-user-id` (mock auth); the real backend uses a token.
- Every status change needs a `rationale` and writes an `AuditEvent` (actor = person or `agent:<name>`).
- The AI never edits directly: it returns `Proposal`s (field, body, question answer, new question, new requirement) that a PM accepts or rejects.
- Only the owner or a co-owner changes a case or requirement. The head of product line signs off and resolves escalations. Everyone can read, comment, watch and escalate.
- Case score = weighted mean of 8 factors (0..1), with no cost. Requirement rank = case score × cost multiplier (S/M/L). Evidence level is separate from the score.

AI that turns customer voice, market data and competitor research into prioritized, evidence-backed requirements for the next BMW, with the product manager in control of every decision.

TUM.ai Hackathon Final · BMW Group challenge "AI for Product Decision Making"

--- ## The problem A BMW product manager defining the **successor** of a vehicle line (3 to 5 years ahead) has to read thousands of customer verbatims, customer studies, option lists, competitor news and trend reports, then argue for the roughly **top 10 requirements** that go to engineering. In interviews, BMW PMs told us research is the bottleneck, and that a tool is only useful if it is **no black box**: every proposal must show its source, market and evidence, and the PM decides. ## What Argon does ``` Signal ──► Case (problem) ──► PM confirms ──► Requirement (solution) ──► PM approves ──► engineering ``` | Step | What it is | Who acts | |---|---|---| | **Signal** | One statement about one feature from one source record (a BMW verbatim, a review sentence, a competitor fact, a trend), with the exact quote, market and source link. Invalid signals go to a visible quarantine. | AI extracts, a validation gate checks every quote against the stored record | | **Case** | A customer problem built from a group of signals, e.g. *"Front seat ventilation too weak"*. Keeps all opinions per market and powertrain, so market conflicts become visible. Scored, but has no cost. | AI clusters, figures and tags; **PM confirms or rejects** | | **Requirement** | What BMW will build, customer-facing and measurable: target vs. today's value and competitors, acceptance criteria, release (next generation, mid-life update, OTA), rough cost S/M/L. Every sentence carries its provenance: evidence, PM context or assumption. | AI drafts after confirmation; **PM approves**, head of product line signs off | Everything is written to an **append-only audit trail** (actor, timestamp, before/after, rationale), from the source record to the human decision. A *trace replay* plays a requirement's whole life in about 15 seconds and re-checks the chain: every quote found in its source, every record hash intact, no gaps, a rationale on every status change. ### Highlights - **Fixed taxonomy, no invented themes.** Every signal is classified into BMW's own labels: 219 topics, 11 aspect groups, 11 car areas ([`taxonomy/`](taxonomy/README.md)). - **Explainable, tunable score.** Case score = weighted factors (distinct customers, severity, satisfaction gap, competitor gap, market volume, removed vs. predecessor, capped reach, trend) × brand-fit multiplier. The PM switches weight profiles and sees which items stay on top regardless. Requirement rank = case score × cost multiplier. - **Reach is not relevance.** Distinct customers and capped reach keep one influencer from outranking a hundred owners. - **Markets are separate worlds.** Conflicts (one market negative, another positive) are flagged with statistics and never decided by the AI. - **Argus, the AI assistant.** A RAG sidebar on every case and requirement page that cites a signal ID for every claim ("no evidence found" otherwise) and proposes edits as diffs the PM accepts or rejects. - **Daily web loop.** Competitor, customer, trend and innovation agents fetch from a curated source list within a daily budget; page content is treated as data, and agents can only write signals, never cases. - **Collaboration built in.** Case ownership per line, series briefs, stances, open questions, referrals, an innovation pool, the vehicle plan and Codebeamer-style export. ## Run it **Demo UI (offline, synthetic data on top of real BMW verbatims):** ```bash cd web && npm install && npm run dev ``` Open http://localhost:3000, pick a persona, and use **Reset demo data** in the persona menu. Demo scripts are in [`web/README.md`](web/README.md). **Backend on a local embedded database (no Supabase, no OpenAI):** ```bash cd backend && uv run python -m app.dev_local ``` Then start the UI against it with `DATA_SOURCE=backend` (API on `http://localhost:8000`, OpenAPI at `/docs`). Tests run offline with `uv run pytest`. For the full Supabase + OpenAI setup, copy `backend/.env.example` to `backend/.env` and see [`backend/API.md`](backend/API.md) and [`HANDOFF.md`](HANDOFF.md). ## Architecture | Layer | Tech | |---|---| | UI | Next.js 16, React, Tailwind, shadcn/ui, TanStack Query; typed REST contract in Zod ([`web/src/contracts`](web/src/contracts), exported to [`contracts/`](contracts/openapi.yaml)) | | API and agents | Python 3.12, FastAPI, background fetch worker | | Storage | Supabase Postgres + pgvector (16 migrations), append-only audit table enforced in the database | | AI | OpenAI chat models for classification, extraction, case pages, tags, Argus and requirement texts; `text-embedding-3-small` (768 dims) for clustering and hybrid search. Every output stores its model and prompt version | Pipeline: configuration → one-time seed of BMW's data → daily fetch loop → signal validation gate → cases → case score → PM workspace → requirement generation → ranking and approval. The full diagram is [`architecture.mmd`](architecture.mmd). ## Data BMW provided customer feedback for the 1, 5 and 7 Series (about 10,000 verbatims), a 2025 customer study, sales volumes to 2030 and German option lists. They are kept unmodified in [`All-context/02-data-provided-by-pm/raw/`](All-context/02-data-provided-by-pm/README.md) and loaded from the original files, so every value keeps its sheet and row. Competitors and 3-to-5-year trends come only from web research and are labelled as external or assumption. Known gaps (no Chinese feedback, US-heavy 5 and 7 Series data, no dates, no study sample sizes) are shown in the product, not hidden. ## Repository | Path | Content | |---|---| | [`web/`](web/README.md) | The Argon UI and an offline mock backend that serves the same contract | | [`backend/`](backend/API.md) | API, agents, scoring, seed, Supabase migrations, tests and reports | | [`taxonomy/`](taxonomy/README.md) | The fixed classification (car areas, topics, aspect groups), build script and classifier eval | | [`contracts/`](contracts/openapi.yaml) | REST contract between UI and backend (OpenAPI 3.1 + JSON Schemas) | | [`All-context/`](All-context/README.md) | Challenge brief, provided data, PM interviews and meeting notes, web source list | | [`docs/`](docs/) | UI solution design, design assets and logos, UX audit reports | | [`landing/`](landing/index.html) | Intro loading page | | [`architecture.mmd`](architecture.mmd), [`database-design.md`](database-design.md), [`data-model.mmd`](data-model.mmd) | Pipeline, database design and ER diagram | | [`plan.md`](plan.md), [`changes.md`](changes.md), [`HANDOFF.md`](HANDOFF.md) | Implementation plan, every changed decision with its reason, current state | ## Team Built in one weekend at the TUM.ai hackathon by [Ghassen Zaara](https://github.com/ghassenzaara), [kechich](https://github.com/kechich), [Ahlem Trabelsi](https://github.com/ahlemtr) and [Amine Cheikhrouhou](https://github.com/AmineChr54).
